name: Plate wider than the film lens; how far the camera may turn or slide
how_found: Lesson 90 (log 29): with a 44-degree plate and the film's 40-degree lens, the camera could turn only about 1 degree each side before part of the frame had no painting (blue in the weights view). Workflows (built place, step 2): pick the plate's lens a little wider than the film's.
final_value_or_rule: Plate 44 deg vs film 40 deg (vertical) allows about 1 deg of turn each side. Push in with the lens (a lens change uncovers nothing). Check the weights view at the end of each move: blue at a frame edge means no painting there.
computable_from: the page's stillShot moves (film camera path) + the projector camera.json
proposed_calculation: Horizontal fov H(v) = 2 x atan(tan(v/2) x 9/16). Allowed turn each side = (H(plate) - H(film)) / 2 (44 vs 40 gives about 1.25 deg). For a planned path: sample the film camera every 0.1 s, cast its four frame corners into the scene (ray to the set's surface), project those points into the projector, and require all to land inside [0.01, 0.99]. Return the smallest plate fov that passes: v_plate = 2 x atan(max |corner tan| / aspect factor) + 1 deg margin. Run it before rendering the plate.
already_automatic: No. The weights view (projected-set.js) has to be looked at by eye, and projected-set.js is not in the plugin kit.
llm_tip: Decide the camera path first, then choose the plate's lens from it, not the other way round.

name: Turn to aim, slide to move
how_found: Lesson 99 (clip 29): a turn during the move slid where the lines meet onto the colliery door at the frame edge and put the pithead out of frame. Lessons 106-107: a turn can't close the gap between where the lines meet and the subject (it moves both). Slide sideways to clear the phone buttons: near props slide more than far ones while the meeting point stays put.
final_value_or_rule: Set the aim with the turn once. During moves the camera only slides (straight line, constant turn). To move the subject on screen relative to where the lines meet, slide the camera or move the subject.
evidence: Lessons.md:384-386, 407-411; film-kit/07 Composing a shot.md rule 11
computable_from: stillShot moves (position and target per move) + subject position
proposed_calculation: In projected or built sets, stillShot should refuse a move whose view direction changes by more than 0.5 deg (target moving out of line with position). Slide solver: to move the subject by dx (frame fraction) at depth z, slide sideways s = dx x 2 x z x tan(H/2), where H is the horizontal fov.
already_automatic: No. stillShot allows 'pan' moves (turns) in every set, and check_shot only reports turns.
llm_tip: In a built-and-painted set, never pan during a move; aim first, then slide.

name: Camera at a person's eye height
how_found: Lesson 100: a camera in the middle of an empty road belongs to no one. On the pavement at eye height, looking down into the drum and onto the seat, the view is a villager's.
final_value_or_rule: Camera 1.5 to 1.9 m above the surface under it (1.7 default), standing where a person would stand.
evidence: Lessons.md:387-389; film-kit/paper-film/tools/check_shot.py lines 22, 478 (eye_height default [1.5, 1.9])
computable_from: the set's ground height under the camera (Blender ray)
proposed_calculation: Placement helper: camera z = ground(x, y) + 1.7. check_shot already fails outside 1.5-1.9.
already_automatic: The check is automatic in check_shot.py (film kit; the plugin copy is an older version). Placement is manual.
llm_tip: Put the camera where a person in the story could stand; only then aim it.

name: Match the camera to a liked picture by landmarks
how_found: Lesson 105 (log 31): 'The lines don't converge the same way' was the camera, not the props. Matching the liked picture's landmarks (wheel hubs, chimney top, gate, roofline, kerbs) found our camera 0.42 m too high and 1 deg off. Fitted, the lines meet within 0.02 of the picture's.
final_value_or_rule: Fit the camera to 5 or more landmarks before moving any prop. Where the lines meet must match within 0.03 of the frame.
evidence: Lessons.md:404-406; Decisions.md:586-587; check_shot.py check_camera_match and check_reference_lines (0.03 tolerance)
computable_from: landmark points read off the reference + the same points in Blender metres
proposed_calculation: Already computed (a camera pose fit in check_shot). It needs a 'camera_match' list in the check file.
already_automatic: Yes, in check_shot.py (film kit; plugin copy older).
llm_tip: When a reference 'feels different', fit the camera first; prop moves come after.

name: In a tall frame, stack things in depth, not side by side
how_found: Lesson 64: three cut-outs in a row were 2.4 units wide and fell off both edges; staggered front to back, they fit large. Soft barrels, crates and a cart in the near corners fill the bottom third.
final_value_or_rule: Stagger groups front to back; fill the bottom third with soft near props in the corners.
evidence: Lessons.md:255-257
computable_from: camera + the planned row's widths and depths
proposed_calculation: Row fit: sum of widths + gaps must be <= 2 x w(z) x (1 - 2 x 140/1080) at the row's depth z. If it is too wide, spread the pieces in depth so each one's projected box fits and they overlap by 10 to 30% of the smaller width.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: A 9:16 frame is narrow: think in depth layers, not rows.

name: Main composition rule: the strong things agree on the subject
how_found: Lesson 98 (log 30): even weight left and right was not enough; clip 29 was as even as the liked picture and still looked scattered. Decision 36: measured, then tested by critics.
final_value_or_rule: Where the lines meet, the brightest 3% of the frame, the biggest near props, the warm light and the cause-and-effect all point at the subject. The meeting point is within 0.03 of the frame width of the subject's edge.
evidence: Lessons.md:380-383, 517; film-kit/07 Composing a shot.md (main rule, rule 1); check_shot.py check_lines (gap <= 0.03)
computable_from: shot_facts (exact meeting point from the camera) + the finished still
proposed_calculation: Already computed by check_shot (3D) and measure_composition (picture).
already_automatic: Yes in check_shot.py and measure_composition.py. The plugin has an older check_shot and no check-shot tests or notice-corner example.
llm_tip: Run the shot checker on every composed frame. Fix the camera first, then the props, then the light.

name: Follow a tool's advice once to test it
how_found: Lesson 108: a helper who did exactly what the reports said found 'lower the lantern 0.47 m onto the seat' would have dropped it to the pavement (the chair had moved). Fixes are now worked out from the support's own top. Lesson 109: one downward line slipped between the seat's planks; now five spots, keep the highest.
final_value_or_rule: Fixes measured from the support's top. Five rays under each prop, keep the highest. Rerun the checker tests (run-checker-tests.sh) before trusting a change.
evidence: Lessons.md:412-416; Workflows.md:225-226; shot_facts.py:228-243
computable_from: Blender scene
proposed_calculation: Already computed. Add an 'apply' mode to check_shot that makes the first fix in Blender and re-measures, proving the advice.
already_automatic: Yes in shot_facts/check_shot (film kit). run-checker-tests.sh and notice_corner_test_scene.py are NOT in the plugin kit (it has only break_scene.py).
llm_tip: Test advice by following it once.

name: Rays down hit whatever is above first
how_found: Lesson 88: the notice board's posts were placed by casting down from the sky; one landed on the board itself, and the other at the street's start because the board's new place hadn't been worked out yet.
final_value_or_rule: Start the ray under the thing; update Blender's scene (view_layer.update()) before reading positions.
evidence: Lessons.md:340-343; shot_facts.py:53, 151
computable_from: Blender scene
proposed_calculation: place_prop always casts from just below the prop's own lowest point (start = low), after view_layer.update(), ignoring the prop's own objects.
already_automatic: In set_dressing.place_prop and shot_facts (film kit).
llm_tip: Cast placement rays from below the object, after updating the scene.

name: Model facing direction
how_found: Lesson 114: the chair model faced the other way from what its turn assumed: at 140 deg its back faced the fire and hid the lantern; -40 deg was right (a critic's find).
final_value_or_rule: CHAIR_TURN_DEGREES = -40 (back to the board, seat to the fire).
evidence: Lessons.md:429-430; assemble_notice_corner.py:55-56
computable_from: prop library metadata (front axis) + target positions
proposed_calculation: Store each library prop's front axis in its metadata. turn = atan2(target - prop) - front_axis_angle. Check by measuring which side is nearer the target after placing.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Never assume a model's front; check it.

name: Stand-ins and near upright things
how_found: Lessons 77-78: a painted room tears at near upright things; boxes wearing the painting keep posts straight on a push, but the background they hide must be properly repainted (a free smear shows on any sideways step).
final_value_or_rule: Pay for a proper repaint behind stand-ins if the camera steps sideways.
evidence: Lessons.md:303-307; Decisions.md:461-462
computable_from: camera path (sideways component)
proposed_calculation: If any move has a sideways step over 1% of the subject distance, require a repainted background (not a free inpaint) for stand-ins.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: A free fill is fine only for straight pushes.

name: How far the camera may go on a painted-over 3D set (plate coverage)
how_found: Log 29: turning showed a strip of unpainted houses at the frame's edge, because the plate was only a little wider than the frame; the push was made mostly a lens zoom. In the weights view, blue at a frame edge means the camera has left the painting.
final_value_or_rule: Every frame's view stays inside the plate's view, allowing a 0.03 fade band. The notice corner's plate was drawn from where the slide starts and is bigger than the frame.
evidence: story L948-949 (log 29), L323 (word list), L1203-1205 (log 32); paper-film/scenes/projected-set.js frameEdge 0.03 (line 521)
computable_from: the plate (projector) camera, the shot's camera path and the set's depth
proposed_calculation: For sample frames along the move, cast rays through the frame's corners and edge midpoints onto the set and project the hit points into the projector. Needed overscan = the largest normalised position found, plus 0.03. Draw the plate at that lens, or reject the move.
already_automatic: No. The weights view (showWeights in projected-set.js) is a manual debug view, in the film kit only.
llm_tip: Draw the plate from the start of the slide, wide enough for the whole move, and check the weights view for blue at the edges.

name: Matching the camera of a picture the user liked
how_found: Log 31: the user said 'the lines don't converge the same way'. The camera was matched by landmarks (winding-wheel hubs, chimney top, gate, roofline, kerbs): ours stood 0.42 m too high and was turned 1 degree too little. The shot checker then gave the same fix by itself: 'Lower 0.42 m; move 0.29 m left; turn 1.0 degrees left'.
final_value_or_rule: Matched, the lines meet at 0.684 across, 0.440 down, against 0.706, 0.424 in the reference. The final camera is within 0.02 m of the best match.
computable_from: the reference picture's landmarks (in pixels) and the same landmarks in Blender metres
proposed_calculation: Already a calculation: check_shot.py fits the camera to camera_match landmarks and states the fix in metres and degrees.
already_automatic: Yes, check_shot.py. The plugin's copy is older (1,807 against 1,838 lines).
llm_tip: When the user points to a picture they like, match its camera by landmarks before moving any prop.

name: Aiming the street at the subject, and clearing the button strip by sliding
how_found: Logs 30 and 31: where the lines meet must sit at the subject's edge. A turn moves that point and every prop together; a slide moves near props more. The notice in the button strip was fixed by sliding the camera 0.14 m right without turning (the checker's own fix; the critics worked out 0.12 m by hand).
final_value_or_rule: Turn first to place where the lines meet (1 degree is about 0.027 of the frame's width at a 60-degree vertical lens), then slide to bring the subject's edge to it.
evidence: story L1126-1128 (log 31), L1056-1060 (log 30); 07 Composing a shot.md rule 1 (lines 52-61)
computable_from: the camera's lens and the subject's depth
proposed_calculation: Turn = atan((x_target - x_meet) × 2 tan(hfov/2)). Slide in metres = shift on screen (as a share of width) × 2 × depth × tan(hfov/2).
already_automatic: Yes, inside check_shot.py's fixes (plugin copy older).
llm_tip: Never close a composition gap by turning: a turn moves everything together.

name: Camera height and level
how_found: Log 30: the two rounds of critics disagreed on the camera's height (1.5 or 1.85 m); a picture drawn in Blender settled it. Seedance's hip-height camera looked wrong. Log 31: the checker had the camera's lean sign wrong (fixed).
final_value_or_rule: Standing eye height, 1.5 to 1.9 m above the pavement under the camera. In Blender, X rotation exactly 90 and Y rotation 0 (level, no lean). High enough to see into the drum and onto the chair's seat.
evidence: story L1026-1027, L1073-1075 (log 30), L1116 (log 31); check_shot.py eye_height (docstring line 24); 07 rule 2
computable_from: the camera and the ground height
proposed_calculation: Already checked. Add the least height that shows a top surface as an oval: h ≥ z_top + d × tan(10 degrees).
already_automatic: Yes, check_shot camera checks (plugin kit, older copy).
llm_tip: Stand the camera where a person would stand on the pavement, never in the middle of an empty road.

name: Camera distance from figures (no faces for the painter) against filling the frame
how_found: Log 34 plan: the waiting workers are seen from behind and never nearer than about 6 m, so the painter has no faces to paint. Round 4's critic found the story small and high over bare paving, so round 5 moves the cameras about 3 m nearer.
final_value_or_rule: Figures about 6 m or more away and seen from behind. Cameras about 3 m nearer than in round 4.
computable_from: the figures' positions, the camera and the lens
proposed_calculation: Head height on screen = 0.23 m × f_px / distance, where f_px = (H/2) / tan(vfov/2). Keep it under a limit set by the people test (about 40 px is a guess to calibrate) for figures facing the camera. Then pick the nearest camera that meets both that limit and story_reaches_down ≥ 0.70.
already_automatic: No (story_reaches_down exists in the film kit's checker only).
llm_tip: Choose the camera's distance from two numbers together: how big faces get (keep small) and how far down the frame the story reaches (at least 0.70).

name: Fill the bottom of the tall frame
how_found: Log 20 research on miniatures and vertical video: low, close cameras; subjects stacked in depth; chimneys and sky in the top third; barrels, crates and a cart in the near corners. Log 26 review: in about 70% of frames the bottom fifth was more than 30% darker than the middle, which came from the painting prompts' rule 'the lower quarter of the picture is the empty floor'. Log 34 round 4: bare paving in the bottom third.
final_value_or_rule: Some story prop or the subject reaches at least 0.70 down the frame (the notice corner's drum, chair and pail fill 0.45 to 0.8 down). The bottom fifth is not more than 30% darker than the middle. Never tell a painter to leave the lower quarter empty.
evidence: story L643-649 (log 20), L829-831 and L847-848 (log 26), L1382-1383 (log 34); 07 Composing a shot.md lines 214-219
computable_from: rendered frames and the shot facts
proposed_calculation: Per frame, compare mean brightness of the bottom 20% with rows 40 to 60%; flag below 0.7. Use check_shot story_reaches_down 0.70; if it fails, lower the camera or move it nearer until the nearest story prop's lowest point lands at 0.70 of the height or more.
already_automatic: story_reaches_down is in the film kit's check_shot.py only, NOT in the plugin copy. The bottom-fifth ratio is not automated.
llm_tip: Fill the lower frame with the story itself, not dark filler: rule 8 forbids a big dark thing in the bottom left.

name: Main composing rule: every strong thing points at the same place
how_found: Log 30 measured the liked picture with measure_composition.py, then five critics and a skeptic. In the liked picture about half to two thirds of the brightest parts fall on the notice; in our clip about a fifth. Log 31's rebuilt frame: the notice 3.1 times the frame's average and 60% of the brightest parts; every strong thing within 0.11 of the frame's width of the others.
final_value_or_rule: Where the lines meet, the centre of the brightest 3% (after a slight blur), the centre of the warm light and the centre of the story props all fall in a box at most 0.40 W by 0.50 H that holds the subject. At least 3/4 of the brightest parts in the story box and 2/5 on the subject. Subject at least 1.8 times the frame's average. Sky dim.
evidence: story L1038-1052 (log 30), L1135-1141 (log 31); 07 lines 25-48 and rule 5
computable_from: a render and the shot facts
proposed_calculation: Already computed by check_shot.py.
already_automatic: Yes: check_shot.py and measure_composition.py, both in the plugin kit (check_shot is an older copy).
llm_tip: Fix the one strong thing pointing elsewhere first; it matters more than any other change. Rule-of-thirds reasons were tested and thrown out (log 30).

name: Story props as one touching group; work props small and far
how_found: Logs 30 and 31: the chair faced the wrong way (its back to the fire, hiding the lantern) and was turned round; lantern on the seat; pail at the chair's feet. Clip 29's sacks covered about 7% of the frame.
final_value_or_rule: Each story prop touches or overlaps another; together they fit a box at most 0.40 by 0.50. The chair stands directly below the notice, seat visible, lantern lit on it. Each work prop covers at most 2% of the frame and is darker than average.
computable_from: the shot facts
proposed_calculation: Already computed by check_shot (rule 9 only partly).
already_automatic: Yes for rules 3 and 8 (check_shot.py). Rule 9 mostly not.
llm_tip: Props that touch read like a sentence; props spaced apart read like a list.

name: Edges that just touch (near-touch)
how_found: Log 30 found three pairs touching in the liked picture. Log 31 removed a far lamp touching the board's post right where the lines meet. Log 32: an over-wide drum lining brought the drum's edge to 9 px from the notice; the drum's side ran 2 px in front of the post for 113 px, fixed by moving the post 4.5 cm. The checker now measures the longest touching stretch and includes background props.
final_value_or_rule: On a frame 1,536 px wide: overlaps of at least 20 px and gaps of at least 25 px, scaled to the frame's width.
computable_from: the flat-colour id pictures from shot_facts.py
proposed_calculation: Already computed. The fix in metres is pixels × depth / f_px.
already_automatic: Yes, check_shot.py (the plugin copy is older and may lack the longest-stretch and background-prop parts).
llm_tip: List background props under pairs_also. Posts running along another prop's edge are easy to miss by eye.

name: A crowd as seen from the camera
how_found: Log 34 round 4: the men stood in single file, so from the camera they stacked into one dark column, and nobody was ever seen working. Round 5: a loose crowd across the gate and people working inside the lit doorways. Log 27: the strike crowd seemed to stand inside the factory until the pavement was widened and the crowd moved forward.
final_value_or_rule: A loose crowd across the gate; workers visible in lit doorways; crowds clearly outside buildings.
computable_from: the figures' positions and the camera
proposed_calculation: Place figures on a jittered band sideways to the view (at least 0.6 m apart across, ±1 m in depth). Check on screen that each figure is at least 50% visible and that together they span at least 60% of the gate's width.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Arrange people as the camera sees them, not as seen from above.

name: Camera stands in line with the subject's edge, never turned
how_found: Design critics (T1, T2, T22) checked the first plan with the lens: W3 placed 3 to 3.6 m right of the lane's middle put the meeting point 0.15 to 0.18 of the frame's width off the pier, and turning could not close it; W1/W2 1 m off the wall saw the gate at 4.5 degrees (edge-on). Log 31 found the same.
final_value_or_rule: Level camera, yaw 0: the lines meet at 0.5 across, 0.5 down. A sideways offset L at distance D moves the meeting point 0.5 x (L/D)/0.327 of the frame width. Stand with camera x on the subject's edge; a face seen at under about 20 degrees is edge-on and fails.
computable_from: subject outline in the 3D scene, camera lens
proposed_calculation: camera_x = x of the subject edge (or centre) that should hold the meeting point; yaw = pitch = 0; check |across(vanishing point) - across(subject edge)| <= 0.02; reject spots where atan(lateral/forward) to the subject's face < 20 deg.
already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py measures where the lines meet after a render (main rule). Nothing places the camera.
llm_tip: To move the meeting point, move the camera sideways; turning it moves everything together and never closes the gap.

name: Street camera sideways spot: clear of the near houses
how_found: Round 2: the plan's spot in line with the outer pier put the camera 0.2 m from the house fronts; near house and downpipe filled about 40% of the frame and a downpipe hid No. 2's chimney. Round 3 compared four placings with the shot checker (mid-pavement 12 and 4 problems; gates moved 0.5 or 0.9 m pushed the nearest man past the phone buttons; the pier spot stood inside the bank's bay). Round 4 moved 0.4 m toward the kerb.
final_value_or_rule: W1/W2 at x = +-3.7 m: pavement middle (4.1) minus 0.4 m, so 1.5 m from the house fronts. The near house then reaches only to about 0.2 across (was 0.28). Nearest downpipes removed; the two nearest cottages' windows dark, one dim curtained window at 0.6 share.
evidence: KIT/.../works/assemble_works.py lines 124-131 and 404-405; SCRATCH/redesign/round2-result.json checked.findings[0]; round3-result.json works.summary; round4-result.json set.summary 'Fuller W1 and W2'
computable_from: 3D scene (house-front line, kerb, subject), lens
proposed_calculation: Search camera x across the pavement in 0.1 m steps; for each, project the near facade's nearest visible corner and the subject; keep near facade <= 0.20 across (or >= 0.80 on the right), subject's far edge <= 0.88 across, meeting point on the subject; flag any vertical pipe or post within 0.3 m of the camera-to-subject ray.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Never stand a street camera against the house fronts; about 1.5 m out keeps the near wall in the frame's outer fifth.

name: Camera distance so the story fills the lower frame (feet near 0.72 down)
how_found: Round 4 critic against the notice-corner standard (drum, chair, pail fill 0.45 to 0.8 down): the Works story sat 0.53 to 0.65 down over 35 to 40% bare paving, because the 6 m rule plus a 6.6 m single file pushed the camera 12 m back. Worked out from the camera: 3 m nearer. Round 5 applied it and measured.
final_value_or_rule: W1/W2 plate 10.0 m and composed 8.8 m from the wall (were 13.0 and 11.8). Nearest man about 7 m away, feet about 0.72 down, gate about half the frame's width. Round 5 check: DIESEL drum reaches 0.72 down in W1 and W2 (target 0.70).
evidence: assemble_works.py lines 132-138; round4-result.json critique.findings[2]; SCRATCH/redesign/round5-set/checks/w1-quiet-d/light/report.md line 73; w2-quiet-c/light/report.md line 53
computable_from: eye height, ground height under the nearest story thing, lens
proposed_calculation: d_needed = 1649.4 x (eye - ground) / ((target - 0.5) x 1920). Target 0.72, eye 1.7 m: 6.6 m (7.2 m if the thing stands on a road 0.14 m lower). Put the composed spot so the nearest story thing's front foot is at d_needed, but no nearer than the figure minimum; plate spot = composed spot + slide length.
already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py's story_reaches_down reports it after a Blender run (film kit only); nothing places the camera.
llm_tip: Work out the camera distance from 'nearest story thing's feet at 0.70 to 0.72 down' before building; a bare floor in the lower third is the commonest failure.

name: Raised eye height for the overview shot
how_found: Round 3 compared W3 eye heights 4.6, 5.5 and 6.5 m with the shot checker. Round 3's check wanted the queue's tail in the bottom third; with the eye 4.6 m up it reached only 0.66. Round 4 raised it.
final_value_or_rule: W3 eye 5.6 m above the lane (end terrace on a 1 m raised footway); last man's feet 0.71 down while still 6.07 m from W1's camera. Lines meet on the wall between the gates (about halfway down).
evidence: assemble_works.py lines 158-164; round4-result.json set.summary 'W3's queue'; round3-result.json works.summary
computable_from: camera spot, the furthest-forward story thing, lens
proposed_calculation: eye = ground + (target - 0.5) x 1920 x d / 1649.4 for the nearest story element at depth d (target 0.70 to 0.75). Check the meeting point stays on the subject.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: For a 'bigger picture' view, raise the eye until the nearest story thing reaches the bottom third, not by tilting.

name: Painted figures seen from behind: never nearer than 6 m
how_found: Plan from the lens (a 1.75 m man at 6 m is about a quarter of the frame height). People test (round 1): men at 6.62 to 8.80 m, 347 to 453 px tall, read 'at once as working men' at phone size. Round 3 set every man at least 6.2 m from any camera that sees him.
final_value_or_rule: Backs to the camera, at least 6 m from every camera spot that sees them (plate, composed, every slide frame). 1.75 m x 1649.4 / 6 = 481 px = 0.25 of the frame.
evidence: PLAN line 124, 1468-1469; round1-result.json built[1].tested table; round3-result.json works.summary 'The men'
computable_from: figure positions, all camera spots and slide paths
proposed_calculation: d_min = 1649.4 x 1.75 / (0.25 x 1920) = 6.0 m; for every figure and every camera position along each slide, assert depth >= 6.0 m; report the nearest.
already_automatic: No; a figure distance table was printed by a scratch script per round.
llm_tip: Keep painted people backs-to-camera and at least 6 m away, measured from every camera position including the end of the slide.

name: Head size decides painted or silhouette (faces)
how_found: Teaching critic T8: at 6.5 m a facing man's head is about 58 px and the painter would paint faces. Round 4 critic: workers inside the doorways at 16 to 19 m have heads of 20 to 24 px, too small for faces. Glasgow walkers at 50 m are about 56 px tall.
final_value_or_rule: A figure that faces the camera or shows a lit profile is painted only if its head is about 24 px or less (about 16 m or further); otherwise it is a near-black own-surface silhouette (page 14 men at 6.5 m), or turned away.
evidence: PLAN lines 124-126 and 1434 (T8); round4-result.json critique.findings[0]
computable_from: figure positions and facing, camera spots
proposed_calculation: head_px = 0.23 x 1649.4 / d. facing = dot(figure forward, direction to camera) > -0.2 (face or profile visible). If facing and head_px > 24: mark 'own-surface silhouette' or rotate away. Distance at 24 px = 15.8 m.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Faces appear when a painter sees a head over about 24 px turned toward the camera: either push such figures past about 16 m or keep them as dark silhouettes.

name: Crowd stands across the line of sight, not along it
how_found: Round 3's fix put the queue in single file along the kerb (1.1 to 1.3 m gaps). Round 4 critic: both cameras look up the lane, so the file was seen end-on: 7 men one dark column in W3, a black mass in W1, No. 2's 8 men a black wedge (2.1% in the bottom-left quarter, limit 1%). Round 4's layout_search tried about 50,000 jittered layouts. Round 5 rebuilt as a crowd at the gate. W4 earlier: from the outer hinge post the 8 men stood behind one another and read as one man.
final_value_or_rule: A loose crowd two deep across the gateway, backs to the lane, 0.3 to 0.5 m between shoulders, back row about 0.8 m behind the front row, each turned 4 to 16 deg, scaled 0.96 to 1.04 so heads differ; drums in front of the crowd's end so nobody stands in front of them from W1 or W3. Rule: never line figures up along a camera's ray.

name: Profile faces turned away from the fire
how_found: Round 2: the stooped and arms-folded men faced the fire, so a lit cheek and ear showed. Round 3 turned them 18 deg (first try went the wrong way and showed more face). Round 4 bowed the stooped man's head 22 deg further and turned it 24 deg so his face is under the peak.

name: Turn first to place the meeting point (rule 1, step 1)
how_found: Log 30 rebuild plan: '1 degree of turn moves it about 0.027 of the frame width at 60 degrees'. Log 31 landmark match found the first camera turned 1 degree too little (5.9 to 6.87 degrees).
final_value_or_rule: psi = atan((u_target - 0.5) * W / f). Near the middle one degree of turn moves things f*(pi/180)/W = 0.0267 of the width at 60.4 degrees. Notice corner: CAMERA_YAW_DEGREES 6.87 for a meeting point at 0.684 across.

computable_from: the across position wanted for the meeting point (beside the subject, with room for the subject left of 0.90)

name: Stand in line with the subject's edge (rule 1, step 2)
how_found: Log 31: the first checker told users to turn the camera to close the rule 1 gap; the verifier proved a turn moves the meeting point and the board together (lesson 106). The fix became: slide the camera or move the subject. Plan 34 defines 'in line with'.
final_value_or_rule: A point P lands exactly where the lines meet only if the camera stands on the line through P along the street: camera x = P.x for a street running along +y. Allowed gap 0.03 of the frame width = 0.03*W*d/f metres at depth d (0.096 m at 4.9 m). computable_from: the subject's (or support's) near edge in Blender metres, the street direction, the planned distance
proposed_calculation: camera_x = edge_x (plus or minus up to 0.0196*d m at 60.4 degrees for a 1080 frame); if rule 12 later needs a sideways slide, check that the slide keeps f*slide/(d*W) <= 0.03.
already_automatic: No; the checker gives the slide in metres only after building (gap pixels times metres per pixel).
llm_tip: Put the camera directly down the street from the subject's edge, then turn; the edge and the meeting point then coincide for any turn.

name: Meeting point height equals the camera's eye height on a street that rises with its lines
how_found: Log 30 rebuild plan: 'the eye-level line crosses the paper about a fifth of the way down'; log 31 checker fix for a vertical gap: 'lower the camera (the lines meet at the camera's own height)'. The board's lift was then set so the notice's top sits just under the meeting point.
final_value_or_rule: Because the ground rises at the same slope as the street's lines, the point beside the subject where the lines meet is always at the camera's eye height above that point's own ground. Notice corner: eye 1.81 m; BOARD_LIFT 0.46 m plus 1.18 m x 1.11 scale puts the notice top at about 1.77 m, just under the meeting point.

already_automatic: No (only checked after building).

name: Camera height and level (rule 2)
how_found: Log 30 critics disagreed (about 1.5 m or 1.85 m). Log 31 landmark match: our camera stood 0.42 m too high; matched eye 1.81 m. The first checker only tested tilt and lean; the verifier added the height range. W3 (chapter 2) looks from an upstairs window, so its check file widens the range.
final_value_or_rule: Eye 1.5 to 1.9 m above the surface under the camera (fix target clamped 0.05 inside the range); tilt and lean within 0.5 degrees of 0 (Blender X rotation exactly 90, Y 0). W3: eye about 4.6 m (5.6 m above the lane), check file eye_height [0.8, 7.0] because the checker measures down to the window sill.

computable_from: the floor under the camera spot (a ray cast down in Blender, or the street model) and the kind of spot (pavement, window)
proposed_calculation: camera_z = floor_height(x, y) + 1.7 (or + 1.81 to match a reference); write eye_height = [floor_offset + 1.5, floor_offset + 1.9] into the check file automatically, where floor_offset is the height of the floor above the surface shot_facts will hit (a sill for a window view).

name: How far the camera stands: the story must reach down the frame (rule 7, story_reaches_down)
how_found: Round 4 critic (log 34): in every Works view the story sat 0.53 to 0.65 down with bare paving in the bottom 35 to 40%; the plan's 'no man nearer than 6 m' plus a 6.6 m single file pushed the camera 12 m back. Fix worked out from the camera: about 3 m nearer (W1 composed at y about 13.2), nearest man 7.6 m, feet about 0.72 down. The checker then got an opt-in 'story_reaches_down': 0.70.
final_value_or_rule: A ground point at depth d appears at down = v_meet + f*eye/(d*H). So the frontmost story prop's front foot must stand within d_max = f*eye/((r - v_meet)*H) to reach r down: 5.95 m at the notice corner (v_meet 0.4395, eye 1.80), 7.30 m at W1 (level lane, eye 1.7). Formula reproduces the pail's measured bottom (0.941 against 0.9403) and the critic's 7.6 m (0.69 against 'about 0.72').

computable_from: eye height, lens, the street slope (v_meet), the planned story prop positions

already_automatic: Checked after building, and only when a check file sets story_reaches_down (off by default; the plugin kit's check_shot.py does not have this check at all).

name: Story group box in metres (rule 3)
how_found: Log 30 measured the liked picture's group; the first checker failed every good frame because the liked picture itself fills 0.46 x 0.44 (verifier); the limit became the reference's box + 0.02 when larger, and the tall board was left out (box_excludes).
final_value_or_rule: Story props (with the subject) fit in at most 0.40 of the width and 0.50 of the height (or the reference's box + 0.02: 0.48 x 0.50 at the notice corner; measured 0.43 x 0.42). In metres at depth d: 0.40*W*d/f wide (0.262*d m at 60.4 degrees, 1.10 m at 4.2 m) and 0.50*H*d/f tall (0.582*d m).

computable_from: planned footprints of the story props and their depth from the camera
proposed_calculation: At layout time keep the group's lateral spread <= 0.262*d metres (1080 x 1920, 60.4 degrees) and its height spread <= 0.582*d, measured across the camera's view direction.
already_automatic: Checked after building only.
llm_tip: Lay the story props out inside a footprint about a quarter of their distance wide; tall backdrops (a board) don't count toward the box.

name: Clear overlap or clear gap between edges (rule 4) in metres
how_found: Log 30: the liked picture had three near-touches (10 to 25 px). First checker used 20 and 25 px on a 1080 frame; the verifier showed the rule says 1,536 px wide, so it is scaled (15 and 18 at 1080). Log 31-32 faults found: lamp post along the board edge for 402 rows (missed until the 'edge run' test), drum side 2 px from the board post for 113 px (post moved 4.5 cm, dx -0.32 to -0.365), handcart over dustbins by 11 px (dustbins moved from y 38 to 36.5), lantern 20 px from the board (passes only just, noted).
final_value_or_rule: Overlap at least ceil(20*W/1536) px (15 at 1080), gap at least ceil(25*W/1536) px (18 at 1080), fixes add a 4*W/1536 px margin; 'only just' note under 1.3 times the limit; touching = within 3*scale px. In metres at depth d: overlap >= 15*d/f (0.038 m at 4.2 m), gap >= 18*d/f (0.046 m). Thin parts under about 6 px (a wire handle) don't count.
evidence: check_shot.py check_pairs lines 961-1062; without_wires lines 112-117; assemble_notice_corner.py lines 117-118 and 252-253; Lessons.md 121
computable_from: the props' silhouettes from the planned camera (GLB meshes projected, or shot_facts' Workbench flat pictures in about 15 seconds)
proposed_calculation: For each pair (story props plus pairs_also), project both meshes, compute the signed distance between silhouettes (negative = overlap depth on visible parts); if -15 < dist < 18 px move the back prop sideways by (18 + 4 - dist)*d_back/f metres away, or (15 + 4 + dist)*d_back/f into a clear overlap; iterate. Use real meshes, not boxes (a round drum fills about 70% of its box).
already_automatic: After building, check_shot.py measures and gives metre fixes; nothing places props to satisfy it beforehand.
llm_tip: Every pair of edges must either overlap by 15 px or more or stand 18 px or more apart at 1080 wide; posts and pipes beside a nearer prop's edge are the usual offenders.

name: Edge running along another edge (edge run)
how_found: Log 31 helper planted a lamp post along the board's edge: 402 rows touching, not reported because a hidden collar overlapped deeply elsewhere. Log 32: a board's panel deep behind the drum excused its post 2 px from the drum's side, so the test became the longest touching stretch.
final_value_or_rule: Back prop's visible edge within 2 px of the front prop's edge (5 x 5 dilation) for at least 40*W/1536 px (about 28 px at 1080), where under 35% of the front edge's band has the back prop behind it, counts as a near-touch; fix slides by need_overlap + margin or need_gap + margin.
evidence: check_shot.py edge_run lines 316-364; 07 Composing a shot.md ('Edges that run along each other')
computable_from: screen x of every upright edge (posts, pipes, lamp posts, board ends) and every near prop's silhouette from the planned camera
proposed_calculation: Before building, list upright edges; for each pair at different depths, require |u_edge_a - u_edge_b| >= 18 px or an overlap >= 15 px over their shared height range; move the post (or its x offset on the board) by the difference in metres (px*d/f).
already_automatic: After building only.
llm_tip: Never let a post, pipe or lamp stand exactly at the side of a nearer object; move it a clear 5 cm or more at 4 to 5 m.

name: Phone buttons: right-edge limits (rule 12) and the sideways slide
how_found: Log 30: the liked picture's notice reaches 0.91, chair and pail 0.96 to 0.97, where TikTok, Reels and Shorts put buttons. Log 31: the checker's fix slid the camera 0.14 m right without turning (the critics worked out 0.12 m by hand); the meeting point stayed put (lesson 107).
final_value_or_rule: Anything to read: right edge <= 0.90 across (anywhere). Story props: <= 0.95 across, judged only in the button strip 0.45 to 0.95 down, using the 90th percentile of their rows' right ends (caps under a tenth of the height ignored). Fix: slide camera right by (right - limit + 0.005)*W*d/f metres, or turn by atan difference when no reference. Notice corner camera x 2.96 to 3.10.

computable_from: the world positions of the must_read and story props' right edges, the camera and lens
proposed_calculation: u_right = 0.5 + f*x_cam/(z_cam*W) for each right-edge point in camera axes; required camera shift = max(0, (u_right - 0.895)*W*z/f) for words, (u_right - 0.945) for story props in the strip; then recheck the rule 1 gap f*shift/(d_subject*W) <= 0.03.
already_automatic: After building only.
llm_tip: Solve the right edge before building: slide the camera sideways (never turn) until words end left of 0.90 and story props left of 0.95.

name: Pre-build camera placement solver (main rule, rules 1, 2, 3, 7, 12 at once)
how_found: Done by hand every time: log 30 helper's pinhole layout (solve.py/layout.py/move.py, which put the camera 0.42 m too high and 1 degree off); log 31 nine 'camera and placing' rounds and 29 lighting rounds; round 3 of log 34 compared four W1/W2 placings with 6 to 8 checker runs a view; round 4 moved the cameras 3 m nearer.

computable_from: the check file (subject, support, story, work, must_read, lines), the props' true sizes (props/index.json), the set's ground and building heights, the lens
proposed_calculation: 1) x_cam = subject edge x (rule 1). 2) z = floor + 1.7 (rule 2), subject lift so its corner is at eye height. 3) d = min(d_max for reach 0.70, distance giving the subject about 3% of the frame) and >= the figure face limit. 4) psi from the wanted meeting point across (subject right edge <= 0.895). 5) project every prop mesh (fast Workbench render via shot_facts.py, about 15 s) and run check_shot.py layout-only; 6) apply its metre fixes automatically and repeat until no layout problem remains (max 5 rounds). Score = sum of check_shot how_bad over layout kinds.

name: Main rule spot box (every strong thing in one place)
how_found: Log 30: five critics and a skeptic; 'hard to vary' because where the lines meet, brightest parts, warm light, story props and the subject agree; clip 29 had three different places. Verifier added the subject's own centre so spots that agree away from the subject fail.
final_value_or_rule: Spots (where the lines meet, centre of the brightest 3%, centre of warm light, centroid of story props, centre of the subject) span at most 0.40 of the width and 0.50 of the height. Notice corner 0.11 x 0.23; Works W3 0.17 x 0.07 to W4 0.30 x 0.27.
evidence: check_shot.py check_light lines 1667-1691; round3-result.json 'Main rule' figures
computable_from: geometry for three spots (meeting point, subject centre, story centroid) before building; the light spots from where the key lights are aimed
proposed_calculation: Predict: meeting point (formula), subject and story centroids (projection), warm centre = projected aim points of warm lights weighted by energy/d^2, brightest = subject if its key light is linked to it. Reject a plan whose predicted spots span over 0.30 x 0.40 (leave room for render spread).
already_automatic: After rendering only.
llm_tip: Aim every warm light at the subject's group and keep the meeting point beside it; a bright sky, a lamp or a lit doorway elsewhere breaks the rule.

name: Subject size on screen
how_found: Log 30 measurements: notice 3.3% of the liked picture against about 0.95% of clip 29; rebuild target 2.9%. Board scale 1.11 chosen so from 4.9 m it fills the reference board's width.
final_value_or_rule: Notice about 2.9 to 3.3% of the frame; screen share = A_m2*(f/d)^2/(W*H). Story props may be drawn somewhat bigger than life (chair 1.05, lantern 1.28, pail 0.85, board 1.11) and keep the same scale in every shot of the place.
evidence: 30 Why it works - checked reasons (reason 2, plan); assemble_notice_corner.py lines 49, 57, 72-73
computable_from: the subject's true size and the planned distance
proposed_calculation: scale = sqrt(target_share*W*H)/(f/d)/sqrt(A_true), or distance d = f*sqrt(A/(target_share*W*H)); record chosen scales per place so every shot reuses them.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Size the subject to about 3% of the frame at the composed spot, and reuse the same prop scales in every shot of that place.

name: Work props: small, far, dim, in the middle band (rule 8)
how_found: Log 30: liked picture's back props 0.16 to 1.9% of the frame at 0.47 to 0.54 down, brightness 0.19 to 0.23; clip 29's sacks about 7% in the bottom-left. Notice corner placed the handcart at 10.8 m (0.9%, 0.54 down), sacks 13.8 m, dustbins 20.8 m.
final_value_or_rule: Each work prop <= 2% of the frame, its middle 0.45 to 0.62 down (fix aims 0.47 to 0.60), darker than the frame's average. Distance band for a prop of height h: d between f*(eye - h/2)/((0.62 - v_meet)*H) and f*(eye - h/2)/((0.47 - v_meet)*H): 6.0 to 35 m for a 1.1 m handcart, 7.2 to 42 m for a 0.6 m prop at the notice corner. Size: area_m2 <= 0.02*W*H*(d/f)^2.
evidence: check_shot.py check_work_props lines 1335-1379; 31/32 reports rule 8 lines; checker_formulas_check.py
computable_from: props' heights and footprints, eye height, v_meet
proposed_calculation: Place each work prop at a depth inside its band and check its projected area; put it in shadow (no light aimed at it).
already_automatic: After building only.
llm_tip: Push work props 10 to 35 m up the street, small and unlit; never put one near the camera.

name: Nothing big where the eye enters (bottom-left quarter)
how_found: Log 30: clip 29's coal sacks (about 7%) sat there. Log 31: a 7.5% black wedge there turned out to be a render fault; the verifier designed the dark-shape test. Log 32: the gutter colour 0.055 joined the drum's shadow into one dark pool (0.16 was a pale stripe; 0.09 kept).
final_value_or_rule: No prop covers more than 1% of the frame inside x < 0.5, y > 0.5; no dark shape (blurred sigma 0.4% of width, darker than 0.6 x the quarter's 75th-percentile brightness, opened by 1% of width, not touching the quarter's top row over 25% of its width, story props excluded) over 1%.
evidence: check_shot.py lines 1364-1379 and check_dark_entry 1382-1421; assemble_notice_corner.py lines 289-299
computable_from: projected silhouettes of near props; shadows need a render
proposed_calculation: Before building: sum projected silhouette area of every prop in the bottom-left quarter; keep under 1%. After a quick render: run the dark-shape test and, if it fails, render once with each warm light's shadow off to find the caster (automatable loop).
already_automatic: After rendering only.
llm_tip: Keep the near-left ground clear and lit; a dark lump or long shadow there pulls the eye away from the subject.

name: The slide: straight, level, no turn, and how far (rule 11 and plan F13)
how_found: Log 30: clip 29's move turned while moving, so the meeting point slid to the colliery door. Log 31-32 notice corner slide 1.5 m. Plan 34 critic F13: K1's and C1's slides magnified too much; 'the painting has about 1.3 plate pixels per film pixel at the plate's spot'.
final_value_or_rule: Start = end - L*unit(horizontal line from the end to the subject's centre), same height, same turn, eased in and out; meeting point moves <= 0.02 of width between first, middle and last frames. Magnification d_start/d_end <= (plate_H/film_H)*tan(film_V/2)/tan(plate_V/2) = (2730/1920)*tan(30.2)/tan(32.2) = 1.314, so L <= 0.31*d_end. Notice corner 5.9 to 4.4 m (1.34, made before F13); K1 1.85 to 1.42 m; C1 3.1 to 2.4 m.
evidence: assemble_notice_corner.py camera_spot lines 349-357; 34 Plan line 1419 (F13) and 604-607; checker_formulas_check.py
computable_from: composed camera, subject centre, plate size and lens, film lens
proposed_calculation: L_max = d_end*(ratio - 1) with ratio computed as above; start computed from end; keyframe location only. Check rule 11 automatically from the camera file (turn constant).
already_automatic: The start position is computed in the notice corner script; camera_audit.py flags turns in a filmed chapter; no tool computes L_max, and the checker does not check rule 11.
llm_tip: Compute the slide's length from the plate's spare sharpness (about 1.3 times nearer at most) and never animate the camera's rotation.

name: Plate lens and size for a sliding shot
how_found: Log 29: a 44-degree plate with the film's 40 allowed only about 1 degree of turn before unpainted strips showed (lesson 90). Log 30 plan: plate 4 degrees wider and 1.5 times the frame. Notice corner and people test plates 1536 x 2730 at 64.4 degrees, drawn from the slide's start.
final_value_or_rule: Plate lens = film lens + 4 degrees (64.4 vs 60.4), 1536 x 2730 (1.42 times the film's 1080 x 1920), drawn from the start of the slide.
evidence: assemble_notice_corner.py lines 89-91, 412-414; Lessons.md 90; notice-corner-paintings.json; people-test-paintings.json
computable_from: the slide's start and end cameras and the set's nearest geometry
proposed_calculation: Project the film frame's corner rays at every 10% of the slide onto the nearest geometry (ray cast), project those points into the start camera, and take plate_V = 2*atan(max |tan| needed) + the 3% edge fade margin (projected-set frameEdge 0.03); plate pixels = ceil(film pixels*L_ratio) where L_ratio is the slide's magnification.
already_automatic: No; fixed by hand at +4 degrees.
llm_tip: Derive the plate's extra width from the slide; a slide toward an off-centre subject moves sideways too, so the plate must cover the far side.

name: Matching a reference picture's camera from landmarks
how_found: Log 31: the user said the lines converged differently; match_camera.py fitted winding-wheel hubs, chimney top, gate corners, left roofline and both kerbs; found 0.42 m too high and 1 degree off. Built into the checker afterwards.
final_value_or_rule: Nelder-Mead over (x, height, turn, lens) at our distance up the street; steps (0.3 m, 0.3 m, 1.5 deg, 4 deg); pass if within 0.1 m height, 0.15 m sideways, 0.75 degrees turn, 2 degrees lens; the painting misses its own landmarks by up to 62 px, so smaller differences mean nothing; the fitted eye is clamped into the eye range. Reference lines-meet check allows 0.03 either way; a vertical difference with a level camera is the lens: V = 2*atan(s/(2*(0.5 - v_ref)*cos psi)).
evidence: check_shot.py check_camera_match lines 556-614, check_reference_lines 659-693; experiments/31 .../tools/match_camera.py; shot-check.json reference.camera_match
computable_from: landmark pixels in the sketch and the same points in Blender metres
proposed_calculation: Use the checker's fit before building (it needs only the check file and the camera); automate landmark reading with line detection on the sketch where possible, otherwise read them by hand.
already_automatic: Yes, inside check_shot.py (kit and plugin kit), but only after building and only with hand-read landmarks.
llm_tip: When copying a composition sketch, match the camera to its landmarks first; never move props to fix a camera difference.

name: Camera too near or too far against a reference (size ratio)
how_found: Log 31 helpers: the checker told users to move every prop when the camera stood too far back.
final_value_or_rule: At least 4 compared props, median height ratio against the reference; if |median - 1| > 0.15 and at least 75% of props agree within 0.15, move the camera median(d*(1 - ratio)) metres along its view.
evidence: check_shot.py check_camera_distance lines 631-656
computable_from: reference boxes and planned prop sizes/distances
proposed_calculation: Same formula before building, using projected heights.
already_automatic: After building, in check_shot.py.
llm_tip: If everything is uniformly too big or small, move the camera, not the props.

name: Props resting where they should (floating, sunk, landed on something high, on their support)
how_found: Log 29: rays cast down from the sky landed the board's posts on the board itself (lesson 88). Log 31: one ray slipped between seat planks (lesson 109), five rays now; the lantern-on-chair fix once dropped it to the pavement (lesson 108). Log 31 helper: a sunk prop read as floating; an upward ray was added. Round 4-5: the stooped man's box reached over the brazier rim, a false 'rests on brazier'.
final_value_or_rule: Floating if more than 0.03 m of air; sunk if more than 0.05 m below; 'landed high' if more than 0.5 m above the street model; a prop on a support rests if its air <= 0.03 m and it hits that group; 'moved apart' over 0.1 m. Rays: 5 spots (centre and +-0.25 of the box) from 5 cm above the base; sunk test looks up half the prop's height; support top from 0.75 of its height at +-0.15 of its box, median. Placing: start the ray low (pavement + 2.0 m, under the eaves).
evidence: check_shot.py check_resting lines 697-775; shot_facts.py lines 221-287; set_dressing.place_prop lines 56-79; assemble_notice_corner.py line 111; works-w1-shot-check.json man_2_note
computable_from: the set and the props in Blender (ray casts)
proposed_calculation: Place every prop with place_prop from a start height just under its own top's clearance; for figures and anything with outstretched parts, take the footprint from the lowest 5 cm of vertices, not the bounding box's quarter points.
already_automatic: place_prop in set_dressing.py (not in the plugin kit); the checker after building.
llm_tip: Place props by ray cast from low down, update the view layer before reading positions, and judge 'stands on' from the feet, not the bounding box.

name: Story props together in 3D, in front of their backdrop
how_found: Log 31 helper planted a drum 1.5 m behind the board: it still looked grouped on screen and passed rule 3.
final_value_or_rule: Each ground story prop no more than 0.1 m further than the support (fix: bring it to support distance - 0.3 m); each within 0.3 m (footprint gap) of another story prop (fix: to 0.1 m); the support within 0.3 m of the nearest story prop. Board 0.75 m behind the fire so it wouldn't scorch.
evidence: check_shot.py check_story_in_3d lines 1065-1115; assemble_notice_corner.py lines 47-50
computable_from: planned positions and footprints (no render)
proposed_calculation: Validate the layout table before building: footprint gaps by box distance, depths by projection on the view direction.
already_automatic: After building only.
llm_tip: Group the story props within 0.3 m of each other in the street, all in front of the backdrop.

name: Words hidden by a prop in front
how_found: Log 31 helper: a lamp post covering 16 to 21% of the notice was never reported; check added. Rule 3: the chair may cover only the signature.
final_value_or_rule: Only the bottom fifth of a must_read group may be covered; at most 5% of the upper four-fifths hidden; a hider is named when it covers over 30% of the hidden part; sideways push = hidden columns' span + 25*W/1536 px; chair scale 1.05 so its back covers just the notice's bottom edge from standing height (3% hidden).
evidence: check_shot.py check_words_hidden lines 842-894; assemble_notice_corner.py lines 55-57
computable_from: projected silhouettes of must_read groups and nearer props
proposed_calculation: Pre-build occlusion test with the same masks (Workbench ids and solo pictures); move or scale the occluder until under 5%.
already_automatic: After building only.
llm_tip: Check words are clear from the composed spot; let a near prop overlap only the signature.

name: Story props cut by the frame or missing
how_found: Log 31 verifier: a pail pushed out of frame went unreported; a prop just past the edge was called 'hidden behind the set'.
final_value_or_rule: Cut if the whole prop's picture touches the left, top or bottom 2 px (the support may be cut at the top); fix brings its box to 0.03/0.97. Missing: off-frame side from the unclipped box (0.99/0.01) or hidden behind the prop that covers most of it; bring just inside 0.05 to 0.95 across, 0.03 to 0.97 down.
evidence: check_shot.py check_missing lines 779-839, check_cut_by_edge 897-917
computable_from: projected boxes
proposed_calculation: Pre-build projection of every story prop's mesh; reject layouts with any story prop under 100% inside.
already_automatic: After building only.
llm_tip: Every story prop must be wholly in frame and visible from the composed spot.

name: Which way a prop model faces, and turning props toward targets
how_found: Log 31 critic: at 140 degrees the chair's back faced the fire and hid the lantern; -40 degrees puts its back to the board and seat to the fire (lesson 114). The board is turned square to the composed camera.
final_value_or_rule: Chair turn -40 degrees (model back on +y). Board facing = atan2(cam.x - board.x, -(cam.y - board.y)). Lantern turn 20, pail 30, drum 25, handcart -75.
evidence: assemble_notice_corner.py lines 56, 108-112; Lessons.md 114
computable_from: a 'front' direction recorded per model in props/index.json, and the target each prop should face (camera, fire, board)
proposed_calculation: turn = degrees(atan2(target - prop)) + model_front_offset, with model_front_offset measured once per model and stored in index.json.
already_automatic: Only the board's facing is computed; others are typed by hand.
llm_tip: Record each model's front direction once; compute turns from what the prop should face.

name: Checker report ranking and the camera-first order
how_found: Log 31 verifier: 'Fix first' picked a 3 px background near-touch over the planted fault; prop fixes measured with a wrong camera would wreck a correct set.
final_value_or_rule: Order: set-up, camera, resting, missing, main rule, then lines, story, edges and light by how far past their limits (past = 1 + min(9, |value - limit|/unit)), background, reference. With a camera fault every composing fix starts 'Fix the camera first'. A failed reference camera match replaces the height and lines fixes. Boxes over 130 x 160 px are drawn as areas.
computable_from: already computed
proposed_calculation: Keep; in an automatic solver, apply fixes in this order and re-measure after each tier.
already_automatic: Yes (kit and plugin kit).
llm_tip: Fix only problem 1's tier, then check again; never apply prop moves while a camera problem is listed.

name: Figures: distance, faces and how they stand
how_found: Plan 34: never nearer than about 6 m (about a quarter of the frame's height); at 6.5 m a head is about 58 px and the painter would paint faces; walkers at 40 to 80 m (about 56 px tall at 50 m). Round 4: single file up the lane stacks into one black column; doorway workers at 16 to 19 m have heads of 20 to 24 px (no faces). Round 1-2: lit cheeks in profile invite faces.
final_value_or_rule: head_px = f*0.23/d and figure_px = f*1.75/d (63 px and 481 px at 6 m with a 60.4-degree lens, 0.25 of the height; 58 px at 6.5 m; 20 to 24 px at 16 to 19 m; 58 px figure at 50 m). Figures nearer than about 16 m keep their backs to the camera or are own-surface silhouettes; stand a waiting crowd across the view, two deep, 0.3 to 0.5 m between shoulders; each figure must clear the others by rule 4 on screen.
evidence: 34 Plan lines 120-130; round4-result.json findings 1-2; checker_formulas_check.py (formulas reproduce the plan's numbers)
computable_from: camera, lens, figure positions
proposed_calculation: Reject a layout with any face-visible figure whose head exceeds 25 px; arrange crowds by projecting heads and spacing them laterally until each head clears its neighbours by 18 px or overlaps by 15 px.
already_automatic: No (the checker counts near-touches between figures after building).
llm_tip: Compute head sizes from distance before placing people; within about 16 m they must face away.

name: Camera matched to a reference picture by landmarks (match_camera.py)
how_found: Log 31: user said 'The lines don't converge the same way'; a least-squares match of winding-wheel hubs, chimney top, gate, roofline and kerbs found the camera 0.42 m too high and 1 deg off; matched, lines meet at 0.684/0.440 vs 0.706/0.424 in the liked picture.
final_value_or_rule: Notice corner camera: EYE_HEIGHT 1.81 m, CAMERA_END (3.10, 17.85), yaw 6.87 deg, film vfov 60.4, plate vfov 64.4; then slid 0.14 m right without turning to clear phone buttons.
evidence: austerity-explainer/experiments/31 Notice corner - working files/tools/match_camera.py, landmarks.py, target_lines.py; film-kit/paper-film/blender/pit-village/assemble_notice_corner.py lines 80-90; Lesson 105
computable_from: a reference picture (landmark pixels) and the same landmarks in the 3D set (metres)
proposed_calculation: Promote match_camera.py into the kit as tools/match_camera.py: minimise sum of squared pixel errors of projected landmarks and line directions over (x, y, eye, yaw, pitch, vfov); print the camera and per-landmark error; feed the result as --camera-at/--yaw/--fov to check-shot.sh.
already_automatic: Only as an experiment script; not in the film kit tools nor in the plugin.
llm_tip: When a user likes a sketch or reference, match the camera to its landmarks first; only then move props.

name: Story reaches the lower part of the frame (rule 7, story_reaches_down 0.70)
how_found: Log 34 round 4: a fresh critic found every Works view passed the main rule while the story sat 0.53-0.65 down over bare paving; round 5 added a checker rule and brought W1/W2 3 m nearer (plate 13.0 -> 10.0 m, composed 11.8 -> 8.8 m from the wall). Lesson 133.
final_value_or_rule: Some story prop or the subject must reach at least 0.70 down the frame (notice corner: drum, chair and pail fill 0.45-0.80 down). Check-file key 'story_reaches_down': 0.70.
evidence: film-kit/paper-film/tools/check_shot.py check_story_reaches_down (lines ~1201-1227); examples/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/works-w1-shot-check.json; assemble_works.py lines 132-138; round4-result.json finding 3
computable_from: camera eye height, vertical fov, the story group's lowest ground point (shot_facts facts.json)
proposed_calculation: Required camera distance: down = 0.5 + 0.5*(eye - z_bottom)/(d*tan(vfov/2)) >= 0.70  =>  d <= (eye - z_bottom)/(0.4*tan(vfov/2)). Eye 1.7 m, feet at 0.14 m, vfov 60.4: d <= 6.7 m (W1's men at 7.4 m reach 0.704). Put this solver in a camera-placement helper and make 0.70 the default in every new check file.
already_automatic: check_shot.py tests it when the check file asks (film kit only); the plugin's check_shot.py lacks the rule. The distance is not solved automatically.
llm_tip: Before rendering a plate, compute how far the camera may stand so the nearest story object's base lands at least 0.70 down; empty bottom thirds pass the main rule but fail the viewer.

name: Raised camera for an overview view (W3 eye 5.6 m)
how_found: Log 34 round 3/4: the queue's tail could only reach 0.66 down from an eye of 4.6 m while W1 kept every man >= 6 m away; the end terrace was put on a 1 m raised footway so the upstairs window eye became 5.6 m.
final_value_or_rule: W3 eye 5.6 m above the lane (camera z 5.74), 30 m from the works wall; queue tail about 0.70 down.
evidence: film-kit/paper-film/blender/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/works/assemble_works.py lines 158-164 (RAISED_FOOTWAY, W3_EYE); works-shot.json views.w3
computable_from: distance to the lowest story object and the wanted 'down' fraction
proposed_calculation: eye >= z_bottom + (down_target - 0.5)*2*d*tan(vfov/2): with d = 24 m to the tail, down 0.70, vfov 60.4 -> eye >= 0.14 + 0.4*24*0.582 = 5.7 m. Report it in the same camera-placement helper.
already_automatic: No (worked out by hand in the plan and the set script).
llm_tip: For 'move up to see the bigger picture' views, solve the eye height from the frame fraction you need rather than guessing a storey height.

name: Plate lens 4 degrees wider than the film lens; turn allowance about 1.2-1.4 degrees
how_found: Log 29: turning the camera showed a strip of unpainted houses at the frame edge (plate 44 deg vs film 40 deg); Lesson 90; the Works and notice corner then used plate 64.4 vs film 60.4.
final_value_or_rule: Plate vfov = film vfov + 4 deg; the camera may turn only about 1 deg each side (40/44) or 1.4 deg (60.4/64.4); vertical tilt allowance 2 deg; push in with the lens or a straight slide instead; check the 'weights' view (blue at an edge = no painting).
evidence: film-kit/paper-film/blender/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/works/assemble_works.py line 170 (FILM_FOV, PLATE_FOV = 60.4, 64.4); assemble_notice_corner.py lines 89-90; Lessons 90; Workflows.md 'A built place, painted over' step 6
computable_from: plate fov, film fov, frame aspect 1080/1920
proposed_calculation: max_yaw = atan(tan(plate_v/2)*0.5625) - atan(tan(film_v/2)*0.5625) (= 1.37 deg for 64.4/60.4); max_tilt = (plate_v - film_v)/2. Automatic weights test: draw the page's weights view at each move end and count blue pixels in the outer 2% border; must be 0.
already_automatic: No. The weights view exists in projected-set.js (showWeights) but is judged by eye; projected-set.js is not in the plugin at all.
llm_tip: Render plates 4 degrees wider than the film lens and never turn more than about one degree away from the plate camera.

name: Slide magnification limit 1.3x (painting stays sharp)
how_found: Plan 34 critic finding F13 ('No slide brings its subject more than 1.3 times nearer, so the painting stays sharp').
final_value_or_rule: Slides of 0.43-1.5 m; W1/W2 10.0 -> 8.8 m (1.14x), checkout 3.1 -> 2.4 m (1.29x); never more than 1.3x.
evidence: chapter-2-inflation/34 Plan ... .md part 2 'How to read each shot' (F13) and 'The moves and holds at a glance'
computable_from: plate size in pixels, plate fov, film fov, subject distance at start
proposed_calculation: max_push = (plate_h_px/1920)*tan(film_v/2)/tan(plate_v/2) = (2730/1920)*tan(30.2)/tan(32.2) = 1.31; longest slide toward a subject at distance D: D*(1 - 1/max_push). Print it per view in the shot plan.
already_automatic: No; the 1.3 figure was stated, not computed.
llm_tip: Do not push a painted plate further than about 1.3x; if you need closer, paint a closer plate.

name: Sideways slide limit (parallax uncovers unpainted surfaces)
how_found: Logs 23-24 and 29: stand-ins and painted rooms tore or showed a free smear on any sideways step; the notice corner used only a 0.14 m sideways shift to clear phone buttons.
final_value_or_rule: Sideways moves only a few centimetres in painted sets; straight pushes preferred.
evidence: Lessons 77, 78, 107; assemble_notice_corner.py CAMERA_END comment
computable_from: nearest painted surface depth z_near along the frame edge (shot_facts distances), plate and film fov
proposed_calculation: s_max = z_near*(tan_plate_x - tan_film_x) with tan_x = tan(v/2)*0.5625; for z_near 4 m and 64.4/60.4 deg: s_max = 4*(0.354-0.327) = 0.11 m.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Clear phone buttons with a tiny sideways slide (a few cm), never with a turn, and compute how far is safe from the nearest surface.

name: Camera spot chosen by checker runs over candidates
how_found: Log 34 rounds 2-4: the plan's spot in line with the outer pier put the camera 0.2 m from house fronts (40% of the frame a house); four candidates (A-D) were each checked with check_shot.py; kept A (pavement middle), then 0.4 m toward the kerb in round 4.
final_value_or_rule: Gate views stand on the pavement, 0.4 m toward the kerb from its middle (x = +-3.7), facing straight up the lane, in line with the subject's edge; nearest house front fills <= about 0.2 of the width.
evidence: assemble_works.py lines 128-131 (GATE_VIEW_X); works-shot.json 'decisions.w1_w2_camera_places' and 'round_4'
computable_from: the set's walkable surfaces, the subject's edge, check file
proposed_calculation: Grid search: for x in walkable positions across the pavement and y along the line to the subject (respecting min figure distance and story reach), run shot_facts + check_shot (about 1 minute each, Workbench) and keep the camera with fewest problems weighted by tier; print the ranking.
already_automatic: No; candidates were set up by hand and compared by reading reports.
llm_tip: Do not trust a plan's camera spot: try 3-4 spots with the shot checker and keep the one with the fewest camera-tier problems.

name: Waiting crowd stands across the line of sight, two deep
how_found: Log 34 round 3 put 7 men in single file (1.1-1.3 m gaps) to fill the bottom third; round 4 critic: seen end-on they stacked into one dark column/wedge (12 touching pairs; 2.1% in bottom-left quarter, limit 1%). Round 5 regrouped them. Lesson 132.
final_value_or_rule: A loose crowd two deep across the gateway, backs to camera, 0.3-0.5 m between shoulders, heads at different heights, a thin rim light from behind (MEN_RIM_ENERGY yard 220 W, lamp 90 W, linked to the men only).
evidence: round4-result.json finding 2; assemble_works.py lines 1214 (MEN_RIM_ENERGY) and the men placement; works-shot.json men_seen
computable_from: camera position and figure positions/widths
proposed_calculation: Placement solver: for each pair of figures compute screen x of head centres (project with the view camera); require |dx| >= 0.8 head widths (or a clear overlap >= 20 px at 1536) and no figure fully hidden; spread men along a line perpendicular to the view direction; report heads countable.
already_automatic: No (check_shot counts touching pairs but does not place figures).
llm_tip: Never line people up along the camera's view; spread them across it so each head shows on its own.

name: Minimum figure distance and face size (no painted faces)
how_found: Plan 34 'People' (never nearer than about 6 m, about a quarter of the frame height; at 6.5 m a head is about 58 px and the painter would paint faces, so W4's men are own-surface silhouettes); round 4 critic: doorway workers at 16-19 m have 20-24 px heads, too small for faces. People test (log 34): painted men from behind work; dark silhouettes over a painting read as shadow puppets (Lesson 137).
final_value_or_rule: Figures facing away: >= 6 m (man about 480 px tall). Figures that face the camera: head <= about 24 px, or kept as own-surface silhouettes. Profile heads lit by a fire turned 15-20 deg (18 used) away from the light.
evidence: 34 Plan ... .md 'People' table; round4-result.json finding 1; design/geometry_check.py; build_figures.py header; Lessons 135-137
computable_from: camera, figure positions and facing, vertical fov
proposed_calculation: px_tall = size_m*1920/(2*d*tan(vfov/2)); head 0.23 m: at 6.5 m = 58 px, at 17 m = 22 px. Flag any figure whose face is visible (facing angle to camera < 100 deg) with head px > 24; flag any figure nearer than 6 m. assemble_works.py already writes men_seen distances and frame boxes; generalise into the check step.
already_automatic: Partly: assemble_works.py writes men_seen (Works only, film kit only). No rule check anywhere; not in plugin.
llm_tip: Compute each figure's head size in pixels before painting; above about 24 px a painter will add a face.
